surfaces.part: packed earth ground with three soot/ash burn patches and a charred stick

answer.evidence: The whole 64x48 sprite is a flat, top-down ground decal. The silhouette is a constant 64 wide on every row, so there is no outline narrowing and no base. The column scan shows only earth-brown texture, with small dark soot clusters near rows 5-9, 20-27 and 36-43 and a grey ash and stick fragment near rows 38-43. There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, vertical south face or side face, so there are no front-face rows. This is the expected look for a flat kind, and it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are acceptable: 5 visible tones per tile (grass 3, paving 7), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the dark marks are tinted brown rather than black. The earth has mottled patches in about 4 brown steps, but only 14 distinct colours in total, and the shading is shallower than the references' 5-6 steps per material. The scattered dark soot blots are small, repeated, near-identical and read as stamped stickers. They have no streaks, per-pixel grain or ramp, and the grey ash heap, charred stick and ember tip are not visible. Overall the piece is a thin brown base with a few spots, and it is thinner than the paving reference. Because of the doubt, this fails.
